1→# Figma Make Prompt: Unearth — Full Website Design
     2→
     3→## What is Unearth?
     4→
     5→Unearth is a web discovery platform. Users open packs of 5 website cards, keep 2–3 favorites, and build curated boards of their best finds — like Pinterest for discovering interesting websites. The product positions against algorithmic social media feeds (X, LinkedIn) and AI-generated content farms by surfacing authentic, human-made, quality websites.
     6→
     7→**Tagline:** "Unearth the internet."
     8→**Target audience:** Curious internet browsers who are tired of noisy feeds and AI slop. People who remember when the internet felt like a place to explore.
     9→
    10→## Brand Direction
    11→
    12→**Dark theme throughout.** Deep navy/midnight backgrounds with vibrant accent pops. The overall feel should be: the internet at night — calm, focused, a little magical. Like wandering through a well-curated museum after hours.
    13→
    14→**Tone:** Playful but sophisticated. Warm but not cutesy. Think somewhere between the polish of Linear and the personality of a great indie game.
    15→
    16→**Typography:** Clean sans-serif. Strong hierarchy — big bold headings, comfortable reading text.
    17→
    18→**Color guidance (starting point, feel free to refine):**
    19→- Backgrounds: deep navy range (`#1A1A2E` area)
    20→- Card/elevated surfaces: slightly lighter
    21→- Primary accent: warm red or coral — used for primary CTAs and the "kept" card state
    22→- Gold: streak badges, special moments
    23→- Text: white headings, blue-gray body, muted secondary text
    24→- Category tags: each interest category should have its own subtle color identity
    25→
    26→## Pages to Design
    27→
    28→Design for mobile (390px) and desktop (1440px). Mobile-first — this is how most users will experience Unearth.
    29→
    30→---
    31→
    32→### 1. Landing Page (Marketing / Pre-Auth)
    33→
    34→The first thing a new visitor sees. It needs to communicate what Unearth is and why it's different in under 5 seconds, then get them to sign up.
    35→
    36→**Key sections:**
    37→- **Hero:** Headline + subline + CTA ("Start Exploring" or "Open Your First Pack"). Show a visual of what the product feels like — maybe a pack mid-opening, or a hand of cards fanned out. This should feel exciting and immediately communicable.
    38→- **How it works:** 3-step visual explanation (Open a pack → Keep your favorites → Build your collection). Keep it concise and visual.
    39→- **What makes it different:** Brief positioning against social media feeds. "No algorithms. No infinite scroll. Just interesting websites, one pack at a time." or similar.
    40→- **Social proof area:** Placeholder for testimonials, user count, or featured boards once the product launches.
    41→- **Footer CTA:** Repeat the signup CTA.
    42→
    43→**Do not** make this a long scrolling marketing page. Keep it tight — the product sells itself once people try it.
    44→
    45→---
    46→
    47→### 2. Onboarding: Interest Selection
    48→
    49→First screen after signup. The user selects their interests from 11 parent categories displayed as visual tiles in a grid.
    50→
    51→**The 11 categories (each needs an icon or illustration):**
    52→Technology, Design & Creative, Startups & Business, Science & Nature, Arts & Expression, Culture & Ideas, Lifestyle & Wellness, Gaming & Interactive, Learning & Knowledge, Media & Journalism, Career & Professional
    53→
    54→**Behavior:**
    55→- Tiles toggle between selected/unselected with a clear visual state change
    56→- Tapping a selected tile could expand it (inline or bottom sheet on mobile) to show 5–6 subcategory checkboxes — all checked by default, individually removable
    57→- Minimum 3 categories selected to proceed
    58→- A "Skip for now" option for users who want to dive right in
    59→- CTA: "Start Discovering" — disabled until minimum selection met
    60→
    61→**Feel:** This should feel like choosing your character class in a game, not filling out a form.
    62→
    63→---
    64→
    65→### 3. Discover Page (Core Experience)
    66→
    67→This is the main screen where users open packs. **This page is covered in a separate Figma prompt** (Pack Opening Mechanic). For the full site design, just show this page in its "pack ready" state — a sealed pack centered with the "Open Pack" button — so it connects visually with the rest of the site.
    68→
    69→---
    70→
    71→### 4. My Boards (Collection View)
    72→
    73→Where users see all their boards/collections. Follows the Pinterest model.
    74→
    75→**Layout:**
    76→- Grid of board cards, each showing: board name, number of sites saved, thumbnail mosaic (2×2 grid of site thumbnails from that board), and a public/private indicator
    77→- A "Favorites" board always appears first (auto-created for every user)
    78→- "Create New Board" card at the end of the grid
    79→- On desktop: 3–4 column grid. On mobile: 2 columns.
    80→
    81→**Empty state:** If a user has only the default Favorites board with nothing in it, show a friendly nudge: "Your boards are looking empty — open a pack to start collecting!"
    82→
    83→---
    84→
    85→### 5. Single Board View
    86→
    87→Viewing one board's contents. Again, Pinterest-style.
    88→
    89→**Layout:**
    90→- Board title and description at top
    91→- If public: a share link / copy URL button
    92→- Masonry or grid of saved site cards (similar to the card component from the pack mechanic, but in a browse/view mode — no keep button, just the thumbnail, title, description, category)
    93→- Clicking a card opens the site in a new tab
    94→- Options to reorder, remove sites, or move to another board
    95→
    96→---
    97→
    98→### 6. Profile Page
    99→
   100→The user's identity within Unearth.
   101→
   102→**Key elements:**
   103→- Display name and avatar
   104→- Discovery stats: packs opened, sites kept, boards created
   105→- Streak counter with visual indicator (flame icon or similar)
   106→- Interest tags (their current selections, tappable to edit)
   107→- Their public boards listed below (if any)
   108→
   109→**Feel:** This should feel like a player profile in a game — stats, achievements, collection highlights.
   110→
   111→---
   112→
   113→### 7. Public Board View (Shareable)
   114→
   115→When someone shares an Unearth board link, this is what the recipient sees. This page works without authentication.
   116→
   117→**Layout:**
   118→- Board title, description, and curator's display name
   119→- The board contents in the same grid/masonry layout
   120→- A persistent CTA bar or banner: "Like what you see? Start your own collection on Unearth" — drives signups
   121→- Clean, minimal navigation — this is a share destination, not the full app
   122→
   123→---
   124→
   125→### 8. Admin Review Dashboard (Internal)
   126→
   127→The founder's content review interface. Doesn't need to be beautiful — just functional and fast.
   128→
   129→**Layout:**
   130→- Queue of sites pending human review, sorted by AI quality score (highest first)
   131→- Each item in the queue shows: site thumbnail, title, URL, quality score (1–100), AI content likelihood indicator (low/medium/high), source tag
   132→- Quick action buttons: Approve / Reject / Skip
   133→- Expandable detail view showing the full AI scoring breakdown by dimension
   134→- Sidebar stats: total in pool, pending review, auto-approve rate, sites added this week
   135→
   136→---
   137→
   138→## Navigation
   139→
   140→**Mobile:** Bottom tab bar with 3–4 items: Discover (pack icon), My Boards (grid icon), Profile (user icon). Keep it minimal.
   141→
   142→**Desktop:** Left sidebar or top nav. Same core items plus the Unearth logo/wordmark.
   143→
   144→The admin dashboard should be behind a separate route and not visible to regular users.
   145→
   146→## Global Components
   147→
   148→- **Site Card:** The reusable card component showing a website (thumbnail, title, description, category tag). Used in packs, boards, and search results. Design one version and show how it adapts across contexts.
   149→- **Category Pill:** Small colored tag showing a site's category. Each of the 11 parent categories should have a subtle color association.
   150→- **Streak Badge:** A visual indicator showing the user's current discovery streak. Should feel rewarding at higher numbers.
   151→- **Empty States:** Design empty states for: no boards yet, empty board, no packs remaining, first-time user.
   152→
   153→## What I'm Leaving to You
   154→
   155→- Navigation style and placement
   156→- Exact grid layouts and spacing
   157→- Illustration style (if you add illustrations to the landing page or empty states)
   158→- Motion and transition philosophy
   159→- How the category color system works
   160→- Any brand elements or visual motifs (geological/earth/digging imagery could tie into the "Unearth" name — or not, your call)
   161→- Icon style
   162→- Whether to include any gamification visuals beyond the streak (badges, milestones, etc.)
   163→
   164→Make it feel like a place you'd want to spend 10 minutes a day discovering something new. Calm but exciting. Personal but shareable.
   165→

1→# Figma Make Prompt: Unearth — Pack Opening Mechanic
     2→
     3→## What is Unearth?
     4→
     5→Unearth is a web discovery platform where users open packs of website cards to explore interesting corners of the internet. Think StumbleUpon meets trading card pack openings. Users open a pack of 5 cards, keep 2–3 favorites, and build curated boards of their best finds. The tagline is "Unearth the internet."
     6→
     7→## What to Design
     8→
     9→The pack-opening flow — the core interaction that makes Unearth feel like a game instead of a feed. This is 5 screens on mobile (390px) and desktop (1440px).
    10→
    11→**Design mobile-first.** The mobile experience is the primary use case.
    12→
    13→## Brand Direction
    14→
    15→- **Dark theme.** Deep navy/dark backgrounds, vibrant accent pops.
    16→- **Tone:** Playful but polished. The excitement of cracking open a booster pack meets the clean sophistication of a modern product. Not childish, not corporate.
    17→- **The pack opening should feel tactile and rewarding** — like something physical is happening on screen. Lean into the trading card aesthetic: foil edges, subtle glow, satisfying reveals.
    18→
    19→## Color Palette (starting point — feel free to refine)
    20→
    21→- Background: deep navy (`#1A1A2E` range)
    22→- Card surfaces: slightly lighter navy
    23→- Primary accent: warm red/coral for CTAs and "kept" states
    24→- Gold accent: for special moments (pack glow, streaks)
    25→- Text: white primary, muted blue-gray secondary
    26→
    27→## The 5 Screens
    28→
    29→### Screen 1: Pack Ready
    30→The user sees a sealed pack, centered and inviting. A button says "Open Pack." Below the button, small text shows how many packs they have left today (e.g., "2 of 3 remaining"). The pack should feel like something you want to tap — give it personality, weight, presence. Subtle idle animation is welcome (a gentle float or shimmer).
    31→
    32→### Screen 2: Pack Opening (Transition)
    33→The pack opens and reveals 5 cards. Design this as a storyboard of 2–3 keyframes showing the opening moment — the actual animation will be built in code. Focus on the emotional arc: anticipation → reveal → excitement. The cards should fan out or spread in a way that feels physical and satisfying.
    34→
    35→### Screen 3: Card Selection
    36→The 5 cards are laid out for the user to browse. Each card shows a site thumbnail, title, short description, and a category tag. There's a "keep" button on each card. The user can keep 2–3 cards — once they hit the limit, remaining cards show a disabled keep state. A counter below the cards shows "Kept 2 of 3." A confirm button activates once at least 2 cards are kept.
    37→
    38→**Card anatomy:**
    39→- Site screenshot/thumbnail (top ~55%)
    40→- Category pill (overlaid on thumbnail)
    41→- Site title (bold, 1–2 lines)
    42→- One-line description
    43→- Keep button (circle with + icon, transitions to checkmark when kept)
    44→
    45→**On mobile:** Cards should be swipeable horizontally with snap points.
    46→**On desktop:** All 5 cards visible in a row.
    47→
    48→### Screen 4: Kept Confirmation
    49→After confirming, show just the 2–3 kept cards with a brief celebratory moment. A board selector lets the user choose which board to save to (default: "Favorites"). Two CTAs: "Open Another Pack" (primary) and "View Collection" (secondary). A small streak counter at the bottom (e.g., "3-day streak").
    50→
    51→### Screen 5: No Packs Remaining
    52→Empty state when daily packs are used up. Friendly message ("All packed out for today!"), a note about when packs refresh, and CTAs to browse boards or explore public boards instead.
    53→
    54→## Component Variants to Create
    55→
    56→- **Card:** Default, Hover, Kept (glowing border + checkmark), Disabled, Face-Down (card back for the reveal)
    57→- **Keep Button:** Default, Hover, Active/Kept, Disabled
    58→- **Pack:** Sealed, Opening (mid-reveal), Empty
    59→- **CTA Button:** Primary (filled), Secondary (outline), Disabled
    60→
    61→## What NOT to Prescribe
    62→
    63→I'm intentionally leaving these decisions to you:
    64→- Exact animation choreography and timing
    65→- Card back pattern/design
    66→- Pack visual design (shape, texture, decorative elements)
    67→- How the mobile swipe carousel looks and feels
    68→- Micro-interaction details on keep/confirm
    69→- Any delightful surprises you want to add to the opening moment
    70→
    71→Make it feel like opening a pack of cards should feel. Exciting, a little addictive, and worth coming back for.
    72→
